channel.title: doyouknow.app - English
channel.description: Surprising facts about UAE, Saudi Arabia, and the world.

item.title: Ain Dubai: Facts About the World's Tallest Observation Wheel
item.description: Ain Dubai, on Bluewaters Island, was recognized by Guinness World Records as the tallest and largest observation wheel in the world at its 2021 opening.

item.title: Cairo Metro Guide: Lines, Tickets, and Tips
item.description: The Cairo Metro was the first metro system in Africa and the Middle East. Here is how its lines, tickets, and women-only cars work.

item.title: Dubai Opera: Inside the Emirate's Performing Arts Venue
item.description: Dubai Opera is a multi-format performing arts venue in Downtown Dubai, designed to resemble a traditional dhow boat and hosting opera, concerts, and theater.

item.title: Opening a Bank Account in Egypt: Guide
item.description: How foreign residents can open a bank account in Egypt: required documents, choosing a bank, account types, and practical tips for expats and long-term visitors.

item.title: Egypt Customs and Import Rules: A Practical Guide
item.description: Bringing goods into Egypt, whether personal items or commercial shipments, involves Egyptian Customs Authority rules on duty-free allowances, declarations, and duties.

item.title: Egypt Driving Guide: Rentals & Road Rules
item.description: Should you rent a car in Egypt? Car rental requirements, an International Driving Permit, road conditions, and why most visitors use drivers instead in 2026.

item.title: Mobile Wallets in Egypt: How They Work
item.description: Mobile wallets like Vodafone Cash and InstaPay have grown fast in Egypt as digital alternatives to cash for everyday payments.

item.title: Egypt's Universal Health Insurance System: What to Know
item.description: Egypt has been rolling out a Universal Health Insurance system since 2019, gradually replacing the older health insurance scheme governorate by governorate.

item.title: The History of Emoji
item.description: Emoji originated in late-1990s Japan and are now standardized worldwide by the Unicode Consortium so they display consistently across devices.

item.title: The History of the Adhan, Islam's Call to Prayer
item.description: The adhan, Islam's call to prayer, traces to the earliest years of the Muslim community in Medina and is traditionally linked to a companion of the Prophet Muhammad.

item.title: The History of the Crossword Puzzle
item.description: The modern crossword puzzle traces to a 1913 word-cross puzzle published in a New York newspaper, and it became a global pastime within about a decade.

item.title: How Do Solar Panels Actually Work?
item.description: Solar panels convert sunlight directly into electricity using the photovoltaic effect, a phenomenon first observed in the 19th century.

item.title: How Passport Power Rankings Actually Work
item.description: Passport power rankings like the Henley Passport Index rank countries by how many destinations their citizens can enter without a prior visa.

item.title: How Remittances Work and Why They Matter
item.description: Remittances are money sent home by people working abroad, moving through banks, money transfer operators, and mobile wallets.

item.title: How Does Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund Work?
item.description: The Public Investment Fund is Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund, channeling oil-linked revenue into giga-projects and a global investment portfolio under Vision 2030.

item.title: The Legend of Pandora's Box
item.description: In Greek mythology, Pandora's container of the world's evils, originally described as a jar rather than a box, was opened out of curiosity, leaving only hope inside.

item.title: The Legend of the Loch Ness Monster
item.description: The Loch Ness Monster, or "Nessie," is said to inhabit a large Scottish lake, with modern sightings reported for nearly a century though never scientifically confirmed.

item.title: Nile Cruise Guide: Luxor to Aswan Trip Planning
item.description: How to plan a Nile cruise between Luxor and Aswan: cruise length options, what's included, choosing a ship, temple stops, and practical booking tips for 2026.

item.title: What Is Mada, Saudi Arabia's National Payment Network?
item.description: Mada is Saudi Arabia's domestic debit card network, regulated by SAMA, used for most in-store and online card payments in the Kingdom.

item.title: How Saudi Traffic Fines Work: A Practical Guide
item.description: How Saudi Arabia enforces traffic violations through the Saher camera system, points, and how to check and pay fines via Absher.
